geometryMethod: Independent analytic circular edge contact; independent separating-axis test on transformed regular 20-gon cylinder and box volumes. SAT samples every actual solver slice. Contact-equation post-step offsets are reported separately.
energyScope: Translation, body/wheel rotation, gravity and suspension spring potential. The stored spring compression is the last force-evaluation value. No drive/regen input in these declared passive fixtures. Energy screens are not a complete deformable tyre, restitution or damage validation.

trace.format: gzip UTF-8 NDJSON; one row per actual integrator slice, with caller step and dt

limits: The 120 Hz product input interval is retained; hard contact can use the same solver at 960 Hz internally. This is not a claim of three pure 60/120/240 Hz solvers agreeing.
The three-width circular tire model is an approximation, and 20-sided rigid wheel stops retain their facets. Tyre deformation, rim damage and suspension structural failure are outside this model.
Full-width finite response and lower penetration do not establish that a real car could safely cross a 10 cm curb at 90 km/h.
Asymmetric 90 km/h 10 cm strikes remain adverse and their post-impact trajectory has not converged. This is an open physical/numerical limitation, not reclassified as normal or accepted.
